definitions.explanation: A plant in the ginger family (Zingiber mioga) whose flower buds and young shoots are used as a condiment in Japanese cuisine. Has a distinctive fresh, slightly peppery flavor.

examples.japanese: みょうがを{薬味|やくみ}にする。
examples.english: To use myoga as a condiment.

examples.japanese: みょうがを{細|こま}かく{刻|きざ}んで{味噌汁|みそしる}に{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I finely chopped myoga and put it in miso soup.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}になると{庭|にわ}のみょうがが{次々|つぎつぎ}と{芽|め}を{出|だ}すので、{毎日|まいにち}の{料理|りょうり}に{使|つか}っている。
examples.english: In summer, the myoga in the garden sprouts one after another, so I use it in my cooking every day.

notes:
Also written in kanji as {茗荷|みょうが}. A uniquely Japanese condiment plant related to common ginger but with a very different flavor — lighter, more aromatic, and slightly bitter. The flower bud ({花蕾|からい}) is the most commonly eaten part.

COMMON USES IN COOKING:
- {薬味|やくみ} (condiment) for {素麺|そうめん}, {冷奴|ひややっこ}, and {味噌汁|みそしる}
- {甘酢漬|あまずづ}け: pickled in sweet vinegar
- {天|てん}ぷら: deep-fried as tempura
- {刻|きざ}みみょうが: finely sliced myoga as garnish

CULTURAL NOTE:
There is a folk belief that eating too much みょうが makes you forgetful. This stems from a Buddhist legend about a disciple of the Buddha who was so forgetful he couldn't remember his own name, and みょうが grew from his grave. The word is sometimes associated with forgetfulness in Japanese idioms.
